title: Cosine Rule
description: Go beyond right-angled triangles. See where the cosine rule comes from and when to use it.
explanation: Use the cosine rule when you know two sides and their included angle, or all three sides. Label side a opposite angle A.

workedExample.question: Two sides measure 7 cm and 9 cm. The angle between them is 60°. Find the third side.

questions.question: Find the side opposite 60° when the adjacent sides are 5 cm and 8 cm.
A triangle has sides 5, 6 and 7 cm. Find the angle opposite the 7 cm side.
Can you use Pythagoras for a triangle with an included angle of 60°? Explain.
questions.answer: No. Pythagoras applies to right-angled triangles. Use the cosine rule here.

title: Completing the Square
description: Turn a quadratic into a square. Make the turning point visible in the algebra.
explanation: Halve the coefficient of x, square it, then compensate so the expression keeps the same value.

questions.question: Complete the square: x² + 4x + 1.
Complete the square: x² − 10x + 2.
Find the minimum value of x² + 6x + 5.

title: Probability Trees
description: Why we multiply along a branch, and add across different outcomes.
explanation: Multiply the probabilities along a path to find the probability of that sequence. Add mutually exclusive paths when more than one sequence satisfies the question.

workedExample.question: Flip a fair coin twice. What is the probability of exactly one head?
steps: The possible paths are HH, HT, TH and TT.
P(HT) = ½ × ½ = ¼; P(TH) = ¼.
P(exactly one head) = ¼ + ¼ = ½.

questions.question: What is the probability of two tails in two fair coin flips?
What is the probability of at least one head in two fair coin flips?
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. Find P(both red).

title: Pythagoras’ Theorem
description: Connect the three sides of a right-angled triangle, then practise with a free printable sheet.
explanation: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle.

workedExample.question: Find the hypotenuse when the shorter sides are 6 cm and 8 cm.

questions.question: Find the hypotenuse for shorter sides of 5 cm and 12 cm.
The hypotenuse is 17 cm and one shorter side is 8 cm. Find the other side.
A rectangle is 9 cm by 12 cm. Find its diagonal.

title: Simultaneous Equations
description: Find the one pair of values that makes both equations true.
explanation: Eliminate one variable by adding or subtracting the equations, then substitute back to find the other variable.

workedExample.question: Solve x + y = 7 and x − y = 1.

questions.question: Solve x + y = 9 and x − y = 3.
Solve 2x + y = 11 and x + y = 7.
Check whether x = 2, y = 5 solves both x + y = 7 and 3x − y = 1.

title: Straight-Line Graphs
description: Read a line as a story about a starting value and a constant rate of change.
explanation: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. The gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.

workedExample.question: Find the equation of a line with gradient 3 through (0, −2).

questions.question: Find the gradient of y = 4x + 1.
Where does y = 2x − 5 cross the y-axis?
Find the gradient through (1, 3) and (4, 9).

title: Fractions & Percentages
description: Move confidently between fractions, decimals and percentages.
explanation: A percentage means out of 100. Convert a fraction by dividing its numerator by its denominator, then multiplying by 100.

questions.question: Write 3/5 as a percentage.
Find 35% of 200.
A £50 price rises by 20%. Find the new price.

title: Sine Rule
description: Match opposite sides and angles to solve non-right-angled triangles.
explanation: Pair each side with the angle opposite it. The sine rule is useful when you know a side and its opposite angle, plus another side or angle. With two sides and a non-included angle, check whether a second triangle is possible.
formula: a / sin A = b / sin B

workedExample.question: A = 30°, B = 45° and a = 6 cm. Find b.

questions.question: A = 30°, B = 90°, a = 5 cm. Find b.
A = 40° and B = 65°. Find C.
Why must you match a side to its opposite angle?
questions.answer: Each sine-rule ratio uses a side and the angle directly opposite it.
